# CLAUDE.md — travel-assist

## Critical Commands

Claude must use **only** these commands. Never invent alternatives (e.g., `mvn`, `npm`, `kotlin`, direct `java` invocations):

| Purpose | Command |
|---|---|
| Install / resolve dependencies | `./gradlew dependencies` |
| Build the project | `./gradlew build` |
| Run all tests | `./gradlew test` |
| Start the application | `./gradlew bootRun` |

> All commands must be run from the repository root. The Gradle wrapper (`gradlew`) is the only sanctioned build tool entry point.

---

## Always Do

1. **Run `./gradlew test` after every change** to any class in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/` — including `TripController`, `TripService`, `TripRepository`, `Trip`, and `TripDto`. Tests live in `src/test/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/` and use JUnit 5.

2. **Follow the Controller → Service → Repository layering strictly.** New features must go through `TripController` (REST boundary) → `TripService` (business logic, `@Transactional`) → `TripRepository` (JPA access). Never call `TripRepository` directly from `TripController`.

3. **Place new code in the correct package directory.** Controllers go in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/controller/`, services in `.../service/`, repositories in `.../repository/`, entities in `.../model/`, DTOs in `.../dto/`. Do not create new top-level packages without explicit instruction.

4. **Apply Jakarta validation annotations to all new `TripDto`-style classes.** Follow the existing pattern in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/dto/TripDto.kt` (e.g., `@field:NotBlank`). The compiler flag `-Xannotation-default-target=param-property` is active — use `@field:` prefix for validation annotations on Kotlin data class properties.

5. **Use `var` for mutable JPA entity fields and `val` for auto-generated IDs**, exactly as modelled in `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/model/Trip.kt`. Do not change `id` to `var` or make other fields `val` without understanding JPA proxy implications.

6. **Check both `src/main/resources/application.properties` and `src/main/resources/application.yml` before adding any configuration key.** Both files are loaded by Spring Boot; conflicting keys will produce unpredictable behaviour. Add new keys to one file only and note which one.

7. **Verify the `generateJava` DGS task does not break the build** when adding GraphQL-related features. The Netflix DGS codegen plugin expects schemas under `src/main/resources/graphql-client/`. If that directory does not exist and you are not working on GraphQL, confirm the task is skipped before running `./gradlew build`.

8. **Run `./gradlew build` (not just `test`) before declaring any feature complete**, because the GraalVM Native Image and Spring Modulith post-processing steps run during the full build and can surface errors that unit tests alone will not catch.

## Never Do

1. **Never modify or delete Gradle wrapper files**: `gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`, `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar`, `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties`. These are pinned infrastructure files and must not be touched under any circumstances.

2. **Never edit CI/CD workflow files** under `.github/workflows/` — specifically `agentic-ready.yml` and `context-refresh.yml`. These are managed externally and changes will be overwritten or break the pipeline.

3. **Never change the Spring Boot version (`4.0.4`) or the Kotlin version in `build.gradle.kts`** without an explicit user instruction. This is a cutting-edge Spring Boot version; version drift can silently break plugin compatibility, the GraalVM native image build, and Spring Modulith integration.

4. **Never remove or rename `TravelAssistApplication`** at `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/TravelAssistApplication.kt`. It is the Spring Boot entry point; renaming it without updating `build.gradle.kts` and all `@SpringBootTest` references will break the entire application bootstrap.

5. **Never switch the runtime database away from H2** without an explicit user instruction. H2 is the only configured datasource (runtime dependency). Do not add PostgreSQL, MySQL, or other JDBC drivers, or modify `spring.datasource.*` properties to point at a non-H2 URL, without being explicitly asked.

6. **Never embed secrets, credentials, or API keys** in `application.properties`, `application.yml`, `build.gradle.kts`, or any source file. Use environment variable references (`${ENV_VAR_NAME}`) if credentials are ever required.

7. **Never use Lombok annotations** (e.g., `@Data`, `@Builder`, `@Getter`) in new Kotlin code. Lombok is a listed dependency but is unnecessary and confusing in a Kotlin project. Use Kotlin data classes, `object` expressions, or explicit property declarations instead.

8. **Never modify `.gitattributes`** — this file controls line-ending normalisation for the Gradle wrapper scripts and must remain untouched.

## Architecture Notes

1. **Standard Spring Boot layered architecture — no shortcuts.** The system is a textbook Controller → Service → Repository stack. `TripController` handles HTTP concerns only. `TripService` owns all business logic and is the sole `@Transactional` boundary. `TripRepository` extends `JpaRepository` and must not contain business logic. Violating this separation will conflict with Spring Modulith's structural enforcement.

2. **Spring Modulith enforces module boundaries.** The project uses Spring Modulith, which means the package structure under `com.vb.nattamai.travelassist` is not just a convention — it is structurally verified. New modules or cross-package dependencies may be rejected at test time by Modulith's `@ApplicationModuleTest` verification. Check for existing module tests before reorganising packages.

3. **H2 in-memory database is the only persistence target.** There is no external database, no Flyway/Liquibase migration, and no `schema.sql` file — JPA `ddl-auto` (likely `create-drop` or `update`) manages the schema from the `Trip` entity at `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/model/Trip.kt`. Adding new entity fields automatically alters the in-memory schema on restart; no migration scripts are needed for H2.

4. **GraalVM Native Image and DGS codegen are active build concerns.** The build includes GraalVM native image compilation and the Netflix DGS GraphQL codegen plugin. Both run as part of `./gradlew build`. The DGS plugin requires a `src/main/resources/graphql-client/` directory with `.graphqls` schema files; if this directory is absent, the `generateJava` task may fail. Keep this in mind when running full builds on a fresh clone.

## Domain Context

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Trip** | The sole core domain entity (`src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/model/Trip.kt`). Persisted to the `trips` table. Carries `title`, `description`, `destination`, and a date range. The `id` is auto-generated. |
| **TripDto** | The inbound data transfer object (`src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/dto/TripDto.kt`) used for both create and update requests. Contains Jakarta validation constraints (e.g., `@field:NotBlank` on `title`). It is deliberately separate from the `Trip` entity to decouple the API contract from the persistence model. |
| **TripRepository** | `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/repository/TripRepository.kt` — a Spring Data JPA interface extending `JpaRepository<Trip, Long>` (or equivalent). Provides `findAll`, `findById`, `save`, `deleteById` out of the box. Custom queries should be added here as needed. |
| **TripService** | `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/service/TripService.kt` — the transactional service that maps between `TripDto` and `Trip`, enforces business rules, and delegates persistence to `TripRepository`. All write operations must go through this class. |
| **TripController** | `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/controller/TripController.kt` — REST controller mounted at `/api/trips`. Exposes standard CRUD endpoints (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`/`PATCH`, `DELETE`). Delegates entirely to `TripService`; contains no persistence or business logic. |

The application is a **travel assistance platform** at an early stage. The `Trip` concept is the only domain object currently implemented. Future domain objects (e.g., accommodation, itinerary items) should follow the same `Model / Dto / Repository / Service / Controller` pattern and be placed in the corresponding packages.

## After Every Change

Complete this checklist before considering any change done:

- [ ] **Run tests**: `./gradlew test` — all tests must pass with zero failures or errors.
- [ ] **Run full build**: `./gradlew build` — confirms GraalVM native image metadata and DGS codegen tasks do not regress.
- [ ] **Check for duplicate config keys**: If you touched `src/main/resources/application.properties` or `src/main/resources/application.yml`, verify the same key does not exist in the other file.
- [ ] **Verify package placement**: Confirm new files are in the correct sub-package (`controller`, `service`, `repository`, `model`, or `dto`) under `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/`.
- [ ] **Verify validation annotations**: If you added or modified a DTO, confirm all constrained fields use the `@field:` annotation prefix (e.g., `@field:NotBlank`) to satisfy the active Kotlin compiler annotation target flag.
- [ ] **No restricted files modified**: Confirm `gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`, `gradle/wrapper/*`, `.gitattributes`, and `.github/workflows/*` are **not** in the changeset.
- [ ] **No secrets in source**: Confirm no credentials, tokens, or hardcoded passwords appear in any modified file.
- [ ] **Test file exists for new components**: If you added a new `Service` or `Controller` class, confirm a corresponding test class exists (or has been created) in `src/test/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/`.
